conclusion_change.previous: The initial collision was caused by a human-driven vehicle, but the Cruise vehicle's subsequent movement created a separate safety consequence by dragging the pedestrian. The later reporting issue is also distinct: an operator and regulator need complete crash information, including post-impact vehicle behaviour, to assess safety and determine an appropriate response. The initial collision, later dragging and subsequent report omission remain separate. Captured evidence and later reconstruction support bounded capture/traceability successes despite report truncation. The NHTSA order is preserved without inventing a canonical crash-report requirement; the represented later OECD revision is not retroactive.
conclusion_change.new: The crash reports omitted material post-crash movement, impairing the initial investigation trace. Internal recorder, decision-basis and audit-trail arrangements remain unresolved. Later framework versions are excluded from assessment of the October 2023 conduct.
